_comment: Real LAFD facility locations used as multi-station dispatch depots in
InfernoEnv. v2 of this file (previously: one depot per resource type,
flat list) -- each station now carries a ROSTER across possibly
multiple resource types, and a resource type can exist at more than
one station, matching how LAFD actually pools units across stations
during a real incident rather than one station being 'the' source for
a resource category city-wide (confirmed: LAFD dispatches up to 30
engine companies in strike teams to major brush fire incidents via the
statewide Master Mutual Aid Agreement / OES system -- lafd.org/news/
mutual-aid-were-stronger-together).
Rosters below are grounded in the LAFD official Fire Station Directory
(May 2021, lafd.org/sites/default/files/pdf_files/Fire-Station-
Directory-May-2021.pdf), which lists each station's actual assigned
apparatus by code AND includes an official RESOURCES LEGEND page
(Section A, page 8) confirming: AE=Assessment Engine, ALF=Assessment
Light Force, PA=Paramedic Rescue Ambulance, RA=BLS Rescue Ambulance,
BP=Brush Patrol (LAFD's real wildland-specific apparatus), BC=Battalion
Chief, E=Engine, T=Truck, TF=Task Force, WT=Water Tender -- these are
now CONFIRMED from the directory's own legend, not inferred (AE/ALF
were flagged 'plausible but unconfirmed' in an earlier pass of this
file/the accompanying research report; both are now confirmed). The
roster COUNTS assigned to each resource_type in this file are still our
modeling simplification (the directory confirms WHICH types of
apparatus a station runs, not how many RL-sim 'units' that should
translate to) -- but which stations plausibly carry which type is now
grounded in that real, cited roster data, not assumed. Station 69, 19,
23 confirmed real/geocoded in the original single-depot version of this
file; Station 37, 71, 99, 109 added below, geocoded the same way
(OSMnx/Nominatim from official street address), sourced from the same
May 2021 directory. Station 114/Air Operations' fleet size (5 medium
AW139 + 2 light Bell 505, only the 5 medium are firefighting-capable)
is confirmed via lafd.org/about/special-operations/air-operations.
Station 99 and 109 were found via a bounded follow-up check for
additional real Brush-Patrol-carrying stations near the corridor,
after the original 6-station model showed trench_crew's count (2, down
from 3 in the ungrounded single-depot version) driving a real
regression on the multi_ignition heuristic-baseline scenario --
trench_crew has a 73% arrival-effect success rate vs. 4-8% for every
other resource type in this env, a MECHANICAL asymmetry (see
inferno_env._apply_trench(): succeeds proactively on any not-yet-
burning FUEL cell and is blocked once fire arrives, unlike
_apply_water()/_apply_rescue() which need active Threat/Blaze present
-- a much larger, more available target window), not just a roster-
size effect. Both new stations passed bbox + road-graph-snap checks
and were added with a real trench_crew (BP) roster slot each.
Per-station notes:
- Station 69 (Palisades): directory lists 'ALF, E, PA' -- E (Engine) is
a solid real match for water_team.
- Station 19 (Brentwood): directory lists 'E, PA, BP' -- carries BOTH a
real Engine (water_team) and a real Brush Patrol. BP is LAFD's actual
wildland fire-line apparatus, a better real match for what this sim
calls 'trench_crew' than the previous purely-abstract mapping.
- Station 23 (Palisades Highlands): directory lists 'AE, PA, BP' --
AE (Assessment Engine, confirmed) + BP (Brush Patrol, confirmed);
the AE/PA side covers the rescue_vehicle role this station already
had.
- Station 37 (Westwood/UCLA): directory lists 'ALF, E, PA, RA, BC' --
a real station carrying BOTH an Engine-type unit and a Rescue
Ambulance (RA), i.e. a genuine real-world example of one station
running multiple resource types. Also a real Battalion HQ (BC).
- Station 71 (Bel-Air/Holmby Hills): directory lists 'AE, PA' -- an
Assessment Engine + Paramedic Rescue Ambulance station, mapped here
to rescue_vehicle. NOTE: this station's real coordinates fall ~486m
outside the project's road-graph coverage (the grid's east edge is
right at Beverly Glen); its road-graph node snap is therefore
larger than the other stations' (~78-90m typical) -- a real but
modest caveat, same category of simplification the code already
makes for every depot (snap-to-nearest-node, no snap-distance
correction), just numerically larger for this one station since it
sits near the grid boundary.
- Station 99 (Mulholland Dr / Beverly Hills edge): directory lists
'AE, PA, BP' -- real Brush Patrol, mapped to trench_crew. NOTE: this
station's real coordinates sit only ~34m inside the project's east
bbox edge (EAST=-118.440) -- the tightest margin of any station in
this file, genuinely inside but barely so. Road-graph snap is
excellent (~23m) despite the tight bbox margin.
- Station 109 (Mulholland Dr / Brentwood, zip 90049 -- same zip as
Station 19): directory lists 'AE, BP' -- real Brush Patrol, mapped
to trench_crew. Comfortably inside the bbox (~4.8km from the east
edge); road-graph snap ~108m (normal range, comparable to Station
- Station 114 (Van Nuys Air Ops): unchanged location; roster count
raised from 2 to 5 to match the real confirmed medium-duty
(AW139) firefighting fleet size -- the 2 light Bell 505s are
real but are used for training/aerial supervision, not drops, so
they are NOT counted here.
What remains a simplification, stated plainly: exact per-type unit
COUNTS per station (e.g. 'Station 19 has exactly 1 water_team unit')
are not a verified real LAFD apparatus count, only the roster identity
(which types a station carries) is grounded in the real directory.

stations.station_name: LAFD Station 114 / Air Operations (Van Nuys Airport)
stations.address: 16617 Arminta St, Los Angeles (Van Nuys), CA 91406
stations.notes: LAFD's actual sole helicopter base, on the grounds of Van Nuys Airport (KVNY). Roster raised from 2 to 5 to match the real confirmed medium-duty (Leonardo AW139) firefighting fleet size (lafd.org/about/special-operations/air-operations) -- the department's 2 light Bell 505 helicopters are real but used for training/aerial supervision, not drops, so are not counted. Deliberately outside the sim's bounding box (~19km north of the study area); travel time is straight-line distance / cruise speed, not road-graph routing, since it dispatches by air.
